hypothesis: Generating three full question-sets from systematically different prompt frames (execution/logistics, scope/goals, domain-expert) should push the model into different decision regions, whose union spans more coverage dimensions than any single-prompt multi-temperature draw — because prior multi-sample configs all sampled one prompt at varying temperatures and landed in the same generic modal cluster.
technique: Three independent RAG-backed on-device FM calls, each using a differently framed generation prompt (execution, scope, domain-expert), followed by a deterministic Swift round-robin interleave by emission order plus near-duplicate suppression (NL-embedding cosine + content-Jaccard) to merge the three 7-sets into one final set — no model-based selection pass.
result: Scored 0.177 on dev-10 (0 wins / 0 ties / 10 losses vs Sonnet), the worst non-error config yet — −0.130 vs the baseline (0.307) and −0.146 vs the best prior run (~0.32). The round-robin merge foregrounded the same top-priority topic across all three frames as near-duplicates, which the deterministic deduper could not reliably catch (nonRed crashed to 2, with the judge flagging verbatim or near-verbatim duplicates in nearly every case); the duplicate storm consumed the slot budget so coverage collapsed to 2, and cross-frame blending introduced pronoun drift and nonsensical artifacts (nat=2). Hypothesis falsified: prompt diversity did broaden per-frame exploration, but the merge — not the frames — caused the failure, and the embedding-based dedup wall (confirmed across exp009/010/020/021) makes deterministic assembly of multiple diverse drafts unreliable. Discarded.
label: exp021
